{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Clean the revenue column: remove commas and convert to float
df['revenue'] = df['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Filter out QA orders (revenue == 999999.99) and refunded orders
qa_mask = df['revenue'] == 999999.99
completed_mask = df['status'] == 'completed'
filtered_df = df[~qa_mask & completed_mask]

# Cross-tabulate channel and customer_segment to check imbalance
crosstab = pd.crosstab(filtered_df['channel'], filtered_df['customer_segment'])
print("Customer segment distribution by channel:")
print(crosstab)

# Compute average revenue per converted order within each segment
# Only include segments present in both channels
segments_in_both = set(filtered_df[filtered_df['channel'] == 'email']['customer_segment']) & set(filtered_df[filtered_df['channel'] == 'paid_search']['customer_segment'])
print(f"Segments present in both channels: {segments_in_both}")

# Filter to only those segments
filtered_by_segment = filtered_df[filtered_df['customer_segment'].isin(segments_in_both)]

# Compute average revenue per converted order within each segment
avg_revenue_by_channel_segment = filtered_by_segment.groupby(['channel', 'customer_segment'])['revenue'].mean().unstack(level='channel')
print("\nAverage revenue per converted order by channel and segment:")
print(avg_revenue_by_channel_segment)

# Compute the difference within each segment
diff_by_segment = avg_revenue_by_channel_segment['email'] - avg_revenue_by_channel_segment['paid_search']
print("\nDifference (email - paid_search) by segment:")
print(diff_by_segment)"}
